outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the full statement has been claimed but not independently checked: OpenAI's 6 October 2026 release (family 039 of openai/math) contains a manuscript, 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces', whose abstract says it resolves the qualitative Nagata-Biran conjecture for surfaces (equality sqrt(L^2/r) at very general points for every sufficiently large r, for every smooth integral complex projective surface and ample L), with Lean files that show no sorry in the files I could read; no human engagement with that family was found four days after release. The other in-window results are restricted or conditional (P1xP1 and ruled-surface blow-ups; one P1xP1 instance at r = 10; a family of instances with r = 2n), and the older events are partial cases or conditional reductions.
problem_asks: (1) Surfaces: every smooth algebraic surface X. The statement does not say projective, complete, or over which field; the literature's setting is smooth projective surfaces over C. (2) Line bundles: every ample line bundle L on X. (3) The quantity: the multi-point Seshadri constant eps(p_1,...,p_r; X, L) at r points p_1,...,p_r. The statement names the points without saying whether they are general, very general, or arbitrary; the literature's conjecture is for very general points. (4) The asserted value: d/sqrt(r), where d is the 'degree' of L as the statement words it. The statement does not define degree. The literature writes the value as sqrt(L^2/r), with L^2 the self-intersection, and the two agree only if d = sqrt(L^2) (for example O(1) on P^2). If d is read as L^2, the formula exceeds the standard upper bound eps <= sqrt(L^2/r), which holds for any points; so the intended value is presumably sqrt(L^2/r). Recorded in disputes, not resolved here. (5) The regime 'for sufficiently large r': there is a threshold r_0 that the statement does not give. The literature's explicit form (Nagata-Biran-Szemberg) takes r >= k_0^2 L^2, with k_0 the least positive integer such that |k_0 L| contains a non-rational non-singular curve; the statement does not say whether r_0 may depend on X and L (the literature says it does). (6) The content is the equality eps = value, not only the upper bound, which holds for all r.

events.what_happened: Nagata's 1959 result for the plane (Nagata, 'On the 14-th problem of Hilbert', American Journal of Mathematics 81 (1959)), which proves the plane instance when r is a perfect square greater than 9. I did not open Nagata's paper; the statement is taken from the abstracts of Nivoche (arXiv 1906.08518, opened) and the introduction of Dionne-Roth (arXiv 2406.11656, opened) and from the Wikipedia article 'Nagata's conjecture on curves' (opened). This is the only case of the plane statement known before 2024 that gives the exact value.
events.delivers: For X = P^2 and L = O(1) only: eps(r very general points) = 1/sqrt(r) when r is a perfect square greater than 9. One surface, one L, and square r.
events.remains: All non-square r >= 10 for the plane; all other surfaces and ample L; the 'sufficiently large r' statement for all surfaces.

checked_by.who: American Journal of Mathematics (refereed journal), with Nagata as author
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the proof (cited by Wikipedia; original not opened)

events.direction: In favour, for the plane and square r only.

events.what_happened: Paul Biran, 'Symplectic packing in dimension 4' (arXiv dg-ga/9606001; the ar5iv page is dated 5 June 1996). Opened via ar5iv. It is about symplectic packing, not Seshadri constants. Theorem 2.B: there is an integer N_Omega such that for every N >= N_Omega the manifold admits a full packing by N equal balls; Theorem 4.A gives an explicit bound N >= 2 Vol / d_Omega^2; CP^2 is packed by N balls for N >= 9 (Corollary 2.D(1)). Syzdek (2007) and Dionne-Roth (2024) connect this large-N threshold with the Nagata-Biran threshold N_0.
events.delivers: Symplectic packing: an effective threshold N_Omega for full packings by N equal balls. No statement about Seshadri constants.
events.remains: Everything about Seshadri constants of ample line bundles at points of a surface.
events.direction: Neutral for the bullet; the packing analogue of the threshold.

events.what_happened: Paul Biran, 'Constructing new ample divisors out of old ones' (arXiv alg-geom/9705018, submitted 21 May 1997, revised 25 May 1997). Opened abstract. It gives a gluing theorem for ample divisors on rational surfaces and proposes a conjecture linking continued-fraction approximations to 'Seshadri-like constants' of line bundles on rational surfaces, verified in many cases by a recursive algorithm. The paper does not name Nagata and does not state the sqrt(L^2/r) value in the parts read.
events.delivers: A conjecture about continued fractions and Seshadri-like constants on rational surfaces, verified in many cases; not the Nagata-Biran statement as worded.
events.remains: The Nagata-Biran statement, which this paper does not claim to address; whether its 'Seshadri-like constants' coincide with the bullet's constants was not checked.
events.direction: Neutral: a different conjecture on rational surfaces, not the bullet as worded.

events.what_happened: The generalisation of Nagata's plane conjecture to arbitrary varieties, attributed to T. Szemberg in 2001. I know this only from the abstract of Roe (arXiv math/0304124, opened): 'T. Szemberg proposed in 2001 a generalization to arbitrary varieties of M. Nagata's 1959 open conjecture.' Szemberg's own text was not found. Wikipedia and the literature name the surface case the Nagata-Biran conjecture (Nagata-Biran-Szemberg in some papers).
events.delivers: A conjecture statement (for arbitrary varieties); nothing established.
events.remains: All of the statement.
events.direction: Not an event of progress; the origin of the generalisation.

events.what_happened: Paul Biran, 'A stability property of symplectic packing', Inventiones Mathematicae 136 (1999), pages 123-135 per Wikipedia (one search summary gives 123-155). Not opened: no arXiv copy was found. Wikipedia's Nagata-Biran article cites it, and Syzdek (2007) and Dionne-Roth (2024, section 1.6 as read through the Cambridge excerpt) cite results from it: a class of surfaces including P^2 and ruled surfaces for which the packing number equals (eps-tilde/eta)^2 for all L ('Theorem 6.A' in Dionne-Roth; 'Theorem 6.1.A' in Syzdek), and a link between packings and Diophantine equations. Whether the Nagata-Biran statement itself appears in this paper was not verified.
events.delivers: Unverified from my reading: cited for packing results and, per Wikipedia, as the source of the Nagata-Biran statement.
events.remains: Unknown from my reading.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published (per the Wikipedia citation; not opened)

events.doubts: The page range differs between sources (123-135 on Wikipedia; 123-155 in a search summary). Not opened.
events.direction: Unknown for the bullet from my reading.

events.what_happened: Wioletta Syzdek, doctoral dissertation 'Seshadri constants and geometry of surfaces' (Universitat Duisburg-Essen, 2005; advisor Szemberg per the Mathematics Genealogy record). Not opened: the DuEPublico record returned a security-check page to my fetch tool. Known only from search snippets of its abstract, which say that for P1 x P1 it studies Riemann-Roch expected curves in the context of the Nagata-Biran conjecture, links them to packing through Diophantine equations, and suggests that Biran's bound N_0 can be lowered. This thesis may be the earliest written argument of Syzdek's P1 x P1 work; the 2007 article is the published version.
events.delivers: Per snippet only: Riemann-Roch expected curves on P1 x P1 linked to packing, and a conjecture that N_0 can be lowered.
events.remains: Unknown; not read.
events.doubts: Not read in full; content taken from search snippets.
events.direction: Unknown from my reading; same work as the 2007 article.

events.what_happened: Ziv Ran, 'On the Nagata Problem' (arXiv math/9809101, submitted 18 Sep 1998). Opened abstract. It claims to prove Nagata's (N_r) for generic points of P^2 (every plane curve has total multiplicity at most sqrt(r) times its degree) when r = k^2 + alpha with k >= 3 and 1 <= alpha <= 2k, under either (i) alpha odd and alpha >= sqrt(2k), or (ii) alpha even, at least 6, and the fractional part of sqrt(r) at most 2(sqrt(2) - 1). The arXiv comments field reads 'Withdrawn due to fatal error'; v2 (25 Apr 2011) and v3 (8 May 2013) are both marked withdrawn. The error was not identified in anything I could access.
events.delivers: As claimed, and now withdrawn: the plane equality 1/sqrt(r) for non-square r in the stated ranges (r >= 10). Not established.
events.remains: Everything else; the claim is withdrawn.
events.doubts: Withdrawn for an unspecified fatal error (arXiv comment only).

withdrawn.what: The proof claim for Nagata's (N_r) when r = k^2 + alpha in the stated ranges
withdrawn.date: marked withdrawn on or before 25 Apr 2011 (v2)

events.direction: Claimed in favour of the plane case for non-square r; withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Joaquim Roe, 'On the Nagata conjecture' (arXiv math/0304124, one version, 9 Apr 2003; a search summary gives J. Algebra 2004, not verified). Opened arXiv abstract. It shows that Nagata's original conjecture implies Szemberg's generalisation for all smooth surfaces X with an ample divisor L generating NS(X) and L^2 a square. It also proves a lower bound for codimension-one Seshadri constants in higher dimension. It does not name Biran or the Nagata-Biran statement.
events.delivers: Conditional: if Nagata's plane conjecture holds, Szemberg's generalisation (the surface statement) holds for surfaces with NS generated by L and L^2 a square. Nothing unconditional for the surface statement.
events.remains: Nagata's plane conjecture itself; the surface statement for all other surfaces and L.
events.direction: Conditional reduction; neutral unless Nagata's conjecture is established.

events.what_happened: Wioletta Syzdek, 'Submaximal Riemann-Roch expected curves and symplectic packing', Annales Academiae Paedagogicae Cracoviensis, Studia Mathematica 6 (2007), 101-122 (vol. 45 per the repository record). The repository record and abstract were opened; the PDF was not readable. The abstract says: in the context of the Nagata-Biran conjecture, it builds examples showing the conjecture's assertions cannot hold for a small number of points on P1 x P1, links Riemann-Roch expected curves to packing via Diophantine equations, and argues that Biran's bound N_0 may be replaced by a lower number, with supporting evidence. A search summary adds an R_0 beyond which no submaximal Riemann-Roch expected curves pass through r general points for an (a,b) polarisation; not verified.
events.delivers: On P1 x P1: counterexamples to the Nagata-Biran assertions at small r (consistent with a 'sufficiently large r' reading); a conjecture, with evidence, that N_0 can be lowered. Nothing settled for large r.
events.remains: The large-r equality on P1 x P1 and on every other surface; the conjectured lower bound.

checked_by.qualification: Authors of the 2024 P1 x P1 Seshadri work, which cites and discusses this article
checked_by.what_they_did: Discuss Syzdek's Theorem 3.17 and say they cannot justify its claim that certain curves compute the Seshadri constant for odd r (fetch summary of their text; not verified against the printed page)

events.doubts: Per Dionne-Roth (as summarised by my fetch of their text), Syzdek's Theorem 3.17 'seems to claim' a result they cannot justify, and their Definition 3.2 gives a slightly worse estimate. The quoted wording is a fetch summary, not checked against the printed article.
events.direction: Counterexamples for small r on P1 x P1; the bound conjecture; consistent with the 'sufficiently large r' form.

events.what_happened: Bauer, Di Rocco, Harbourne, Kapustka, Knutsen, Syzdek, Szemberg, 'A primer on Seshadri constants' (arXiv 0810.0728, v1 4 Oct 2008, v2 1 Jul 2010; published Contemp. Math. 496 (2009) per the fetch summary). Survey. Opened the arXiv abstract and the ar5iv HTML, read in chunks by a summarising fetch tool. Its section 6.1 ('Bounds on arbitrary surfaces'), Theorem 6.1.10 ('Maximality of multi-point Seshadri constants'), as read through that tool: for a smooth surface S and a very ample L, if r >= L^2 and sqrt(r L^2) is an integer, then the multi-point Seshadri constant at the points of a Zariski-open set of r-tuples equals sqrt(L^2/r). Section 3 notes that the plane Nagata conjecture holds for square r. I did not find a verbatim Nagata-Biran-Szemberg statement in the parts I could read; the attribution of Theorem 6.1.10 was not checked.
events.revisions: v2 1 Jul 2010 (numbering matches the printed version, per the abstract page).
events.delivers: Equality sqrt(L^2/r) on any smooth surface for those r with r >= L^2 and r L^2 a perfect square, at general points (a Zariski-open set). Restricted to a sparse set of r.
events.remains: All r for which r L^2 is not a square; the 'sufficiently large r' statement for all r.
events.doubts: Theorem 6.1.10 is read through a summarising fetch tool, not quoted from the printed text.
events.direction: In favour, for the restricted set of r described.

events.what_happened: Krishna Hanumanthu, 'Seshadri constants on surfaces with Picard number 1' (arXiv 1608.04476, v1 16 Aug 2016, v2 19 Oct 2016; listed as to appear in Manuscripta Math.). Opened abstract page and ar5iv HTML. Theorem 2.1: for X with Picard number 1 and L its ample generator, and r >= 2, either eps(L,r) >= sqrt((r+2)/(r+3)) sqrt(L^2/r), or a reduced irreducible curve C in |dL| passes through s <= r very general points with eps = d L^2 / s; a case (r, L^2) = (2,6) gives eps >= 3/2. Remark 2.2 concludes that eps is arbitrarily close to the optimal value as r tends to infinity, and names the 'Nagata-Biran-Szemberg Conjecture'.
events.delivers: For Picard-number-1 surfaces: a lower bound within the factor sqrt((r+2)/(r+3)) of sqrt(L^2/r), unless a special curve exists; so the constant is asymptotically close to the Nagata-Biran value. Equality is not established.
events.remains: Exact equality for large r on Picard-number-1 surfaces (in the exceptional-curve case); all surfaces with Picard number at least 2.
events.direction: In favour of the asymptotic (not the equality); partial.

events.what_happened: Krishna Hanumanthu and Alapan Mukhopadhyay, 'Multi-point Seshadri constants on ruled surfaces' (arXiv 1610.07812, v1 25 Oct 2016, v2 24 Jan 2017). Opened the abstract page. It proves a lower bound for eps(X, L, r) on any surface for r >= 3 and makes computations on ruled surfaces. The theorem text was not readable (the PDF failed to extract). The abstract does not mention large r, sqrt(L^2/r), Nagata or Nagata-Biran-Szemberg.
events.delivers: Per the abstract only: a general lower bound for multi-point Seshadri constants for r >= 3, and computations on ruled surfaces. Whether it reaches the Nagata-Biran value was not established.
events.remains: Unknown from my reading.
events.direction: Unknown from my reading.

events.what_happened: Stephanie Nivoche, 'Transcendental versions in C^n of the Nagata conjecture' (arXiv 1906.08518, v1 20 Jun 2019; to appear Ann. Inst. Fourier, published 2021). Opened abstract. It formulates transcendental (pluripotential) versions of the Nagata conjecture in C^n, equivalent to a version in C^n. It restates that the plane conjecture holds for square r (Nagata 1959) and is open for every non-square r >= 10.
events.revisions: v1 only in the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: An analytic analogue of the plane Nagata conjecture in C^n. A different question from the surface statement.
events.remains: The Nagata-Biran statement is untouched.
events.direction: Not bearing on the bullet: an analogue in a different setting.

events.what_happened: Dumnicki, Harbourne, Kuronya, Roe, Szemberg, 'Very general monomial valuations of P^2 and a Nagata type conjecture' (arXiv 1312.5549, v1 19 Dec 2013, v2 5 Feb 2016). Opened abstract page. Valuation-theoretic multi-point Seshadri constants for P^2 with real s >= 1 points; a Nagata-type conjecture is predicted valid for s >= 8 + 1/36, and constants are computed for s <= 7 + 1/9. It does not mention Biran or the surface statement.
events.delivers: A valuation version for P^2 with real numbers of points. A different question.
events.remains: The Nagata-Biran statement.
events.direction: Not bearing on the bullet: valuative variant on P^2.

events.what_happened: Galindo, Monserrat, Moreno-Avila, Moyano-Fernandez, 'On the valuative Nagata conjecture' (arXiv 2208.11041, v1 23 Aug 2022; a search summary says Research in Mathematical Sciences 2025, not verified). Opened abstract. Equivalent conditions for a plane divisorial valuation on a smooth projective surface to be minimal with respect to an ample divisor, involving a valuative Seshadri constant; several equivalent statements of the valuative Nagata conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 only in the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Equivalences for a valuative version. A different question.
events.remains: The Nagata-Biran statement.
events.direction: Not bearing on the bullet: valuative variant.

events.what_happened: Hanumanthu, Jacob, Suhas B. N., Singh, 'Seshadri constants on blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces' (arXiv 2312.14555, v1 22 Dec 2023, v2 9 Jan 2024, v3 25 Oct 2024; to appear Math. Nachr.). Opened abstract and fetch summary. It computes Seshadri constants of an ample L on the blow-up of F_e at r points: at an arbitrary point for r <= e-1, and at a very general point for r = e or e+1; it discusses conjectures on linear systems. No Nagata or Nagata-Biran mention in the parts read.
events.revisions: v2 9 Jan 2024 and v3 25 Oct 2024 (after the frozen revision date for v2 and v3).
events.delivers: Exact values for small r on Hirzebruch blow-ups (r <= e+1). Not the large-r regime.
events.remains: Large r; the Nagata-Biran statement.
events.direction: Not bearing on the bullet's large-r regime.

events.what_happened: Cyril J. Jacob, 'Lower bounds for Seshadri constants on blow ups of P^2' (arXiv 2404.11906, v1 18 Apr 2024, v2 7 May 2024, v3 12 Sep 2025). Opened abstract. It studies lower bounds for Seshadri constants of ample line bundles on the blow-up of P^2 at r points, in three cases: points on a curve of degree at most 3, r <= 8, and very general points, where a bound of 1/2 is shown conditional on the Strong SHGH conjecture. The abstract does not state whether the constant is taken at one point or at r points.
events.delivers: Lower-bound results on blow-ups of P^2, with the very-general-points bound conditional. Read as a multi-point statement for L = H with r >= 5 the bound 1/2 would contradict the upper bound 1/sqrt(r), so the bound must be one-point or differently normalised; I could not confirm this from the full text.
events.remains: The Nagata-Biran statement; the abstract's own cases do not address large-r equality.
events.doubts: Point count unclear from the abstract; conditional on Strong SHGH.
events.direction: Not bearing on the large-r equality; conditional lower bound.

events.what_happened: Chris Dionne and Mike Roth, 'Seshadri constants on P^1 x P^1, and applications to the symplectic packing problem' (arXiv 2406.11656, v1 17 Jun 2024, v2 15 Oct 2024). Published in Forum of Mathematics, Sigma 13 (2025), e191, online 21 Nov 2025 (DOI 10.1017/fms.2025.10137). Opened the arXiv abstract, the Cambridge Core article page, and excerpts of the full text via the Cambridge core-reader (sections 1 to 1.9; later pages not read). Theorem 1.1 gives r-point Seshadri constants for 'outer' line bundles on P^1 x P^1 with separate odd and even r; Theorem 1.2 gives packing numbers. Section 1.8 states the equality eps_r(L) = eta_r(L) = sqrt(L^2/r) for classes O(e1,e2) of a square-zero form only conditionally, 'if this description of the nef cone is correct'; the constructions in sections 9 and 10 were not read. Section 1.9 asks for an r_0 beyond which the packing number is 1 (the analogue of Biran's N_0).
events.revisions: v2 15 Oct 2024 (minor wording edits, per the abstract page); published 2025.
events.delivers: On P^1 x P^1 only: exact r-point Seshadri constants for outer line bundles (Theorem 1.1); explicit packing numbers (Theorem 1.2). The sqrt(L^2/r) equality for some further classes is stated conditionally on a nef-cone description (section 1.8). Nothing unconditional for large r on inner bundles in the parts read.
events.remains: Unconditional large-r equality for inner bundles on P^1 x P^1 (as far as the parts read show); every other surface; the nef-cone description used in section 1.8; the r_0 question in section 1.9.

checked_by.who: Forum of Mathematics, Sigma (journal of record; referee names not shown on the page)

events.doubts: Section 1.8 is conditional on a nef-cone description the authors introduce with the words 'if this description is correct'; the constructions in sections 9 and 10 were not read. The authors also say the Nagata conjecture remains open for every non-square r >= 10 (their introduction).
events.direction: Exact values on P^1 x P^1 for outer bundles; NB-form equality for some classes conditionally; consistent with the conjecture where it applies.

events.what_happened: Krishna Hanumanthu, Cyril J. Jacob, Suhas B. N., Amit Kumar Singh, 'Rationality of Seshadri constants on blow-ups of ruled surfaces' (arXiv 2407.18678, one version, 26 Jul 2024). Opened abstract and the HTML of v1. Conjecture 2.5 is the Nagata-Biran-Szemberg statement with threshold r >= k_0^2 L^2 (very general points). Conjecture 2.1 (negative curves on blow-ups of ruled surfaces) and Conjecture 2.3 are shown equivalent (Prop 2.4). Proposition 2.7, conditional on Conjecture 2.1, treats a fixed ample L = a Gamma_e + b f on the blow-up of F_e at very general points and states equality for sufficiently large r; the proof, as I read it, establishes the inequality L.C >= (sum of multiplicities) sqrt(L^2/r) for large r. Theorem 3.4 (conditional) gives the one-point value eps(X_r, L, x) = sqrt(L^2); Theorem 3.6 (conditional) gives an irrational one-point example. Unconditional content: Prop 2.4 and Prop 3.3. A search summary said the paper shows a Nagata-Biran-Szemberg-type statement for any smooth projective surface follows from the ruled-surface conjecture; the fetched text ties the statement to blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces only, so I went with the fetched text.
events.delivers: Conditional on Conjecture 2.1 (a classification of negative curves on blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces at very general points): the Nagata-Biran-type inequality, for a fixed ample L on those blow-ups and r large (depending on L). Unconditionally, nothing that settles the statement.
events.remains: The unconditional statement for these surfaces; all other surfaces; Conjecture 2.1 itself.
events.doubts: Conditional on Conjecture 2.1. Proposition 2.7 as written states equality, while the proof, as I read it, gives the inequality form.
events.direction: Conditional reduction; consistent with the conjecture where it applies.
events.object: A one-point example: an irrational one-point Seshadri constant on a blow-up of a ruled surface (conditional on Conjecture 2.1). Not a multi-point object for the bullet.

sources: https://arxiv.org/html/2407.18678v1 (acknowledgements: Infosys Foundation; NBHM and DAE grant; no AI mention)

events.what_happened: Cyril J. Jacob, Bivas Khan, Ronnie Sebastian, 'Seshadri constants and negative curves on blowups of ruled surfaces' (arXiv 2501.05065, one version, 9 Jan 2025). Opened abstract. Seshadri constants of ample line bundles on the blow-up of a Hirzebruch surface F_e at r <= e+3 very general points; decomposable ruled surfaces over curves of positive genus; bounded negativity. Nagata and Nagata-Biran are not mentioned.
events.delivers: Multi-point values at very general points for r <= e+3 on blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces. Small r relative to the surface; a different regime.
events.remains: Large r; the Nagata-Biran statement.
events.direction: Not bearing on the large-r regime.

events.what_happened: Linus Rosler, 'On Seshadri constants of adjoint divisors on surfaces and threefolds in arbitrary characteristic' (arXiv 2601.16094, v1 22 Jan 2026, v2 25 Jan 2026). Opened abstract. Single-point lower bounds for adjoint divisors (for example eps(K_X + 4A; x) >= 3/4 on surfaces) in arbitrary characteristic; a threefold bound. Nagata and Nagata-Biran are not mentioned.
events.delivers: Single-point bounds for adjoint divisors. A different question.
events.remains: The Nagata-Biran statement.
events.direction: Not bearing on the bullet.

events.what_happened: Antonio Laface and Luca Ugaglia, 'Irrational Seshadri constants from dihedral orbits' (arXiv 2609.26521, v1 22 Sep 2026, v2 25 Sep 2026). Opened abstract. It constructs an irrational one-point Seshadri constant on the blow-up of P^2 at nine very general points (eps(L; x) = 2 sqrt(5)). To prove it, it establishes that eps(O_{P1xP1}(1,1); ten very general points) = 1/sqrt(5), 'completing the reflection approach proposed by Dionne and Roth for the ten-point case', and that the same equality holds at a very general free orbit of a dihedral group of order ten.
events.delivers: One instance of the Nagata-Biran value: on P^1 x P^1 with L = O(1,1) (L^2 = 2) at r = 10 very general points, eps = 1/sqrt(5) = sqrt(L^2/r). A single (surface, line bundle, r) instance, not a large-r statement. The irrational one-point result is a different question.
events.remains: The large-r statement for any fixed L; all other surfaces and bundles.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at one instance.
events.object: Not a counterexample: the ten-point equality on P^1 x P^1 with O(1,1), and an irrational one-point constant on the blow-up of P^2 at nine very general points, L = 9H - 3(E_1+...+E_5) - 2(E_6+...+E_9), eps = 2 sqrt(5). Abstract only read.

sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26521 (abstract only; full text not read)

events.what_happened: Grzegorz Malara, Lukasz Merta, Justyna Szpond, Marcin Zielinski, 'Dihedral reflections and an infinite series of irrational Seshadri constants' (arXiv 2610.01783, v1 1 Oct 2026). Opened abstract. For each odd n >= 5, on P^1 x P^1, eps(O(n-4,1); 2n very general points) = sqrt((n-4)/n), a dihedral-orbit version included; the line bundle depends on n and r = 2n. For odd n >= 7 they also give a one-point irrational example on the blow-up of P^2 at (n+13)/2 points with eps = 2 sqrt(n(n-4)).
events.delivers: A family of single instances: at r = 2n very general points on P^1 x P^1, with L = O(n-4,1) (L^2 = 2(n-4)), eps = sqrt(L^2/r). Each instance has its own L and r; this is not a fixed L with large r.
events.remains: The fixed-L, large-r statement; all other surfaces and bundles.
events.direction: Consistent with the conjecture at each instance; not a large-r statement.

sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01783 (abstract only; full text not read)

events.what_happened: OpenAI's openai/math repository, released 6 Oct 2026, contains family 039, 'Nagata's conjecture and maximal Seshadri constants' (overview.tex, Lean-formalised). Its manuscript 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces' (directory dated September 23, 2026; author line 'OpenAI'; build/main.tex read) has the abstract: 'We prove that, for every smooth integral complex projective surface S and every ample line bundle L, the multipoint Seshadri constant at r very general points equals sqrt(L^2/r) for every sufficiently large integer r. This resolves positively the qualitative Nagata--Biran conjecture for surfaces.' The Lean file lean/OAI/AlgebraicGeometry/Seshadri/Main.lean has theorem maximalSeshadriConstants (S : Surface) (L : LineBundle S.scheme) (hL : LineBundle.IsAmple S.scheme L) : EventualMaximalSeshadri S L. Definitions.lean has EventualSeshadriEquality with seshadriConstant S L r p = Real.sqrt ((selfIntersection S L : ℝ) / r). The Lean scope note (lean/docs/039.md) says the threshold 'is not explicit or uniform over all surfaces'. I did not read the manuscript's section files (introduction, jets, node, compression, lattice, nef), and the PDF was not readable through my tool.
events.revisions: Manuscript header dated 23 Sep 2026. The repository history log (history.md) records only an Oct 7 entry (withdrawals and revisions in other families), and that entry does not mention family 039; the current family listing shows no revision or withdrawal for this manuscript.
events.delivers: Claimed, as stated by the authors: for every smooth integral complex projective surface S and ample L there is r_0 (depending on S and L; not explicit or uniform per the Lean scope note) such that for every r >= r_0 the multi-point Seshadri constant at very general r-tuples equals sqrt(L^2/r). The Lean definition asserts closed exceptional sets Z_n of configurations, with the equality holding off them. The normalisation sqrt(L^2/r) matches the literature. The equality is for very general configurations, not for every configuration.
events.remains: (i) An explicit or uniform threshold such as r >= k_0^2 L^2 (the Nagata-Biran-Szemberg form in the literature). (ii) Equality for every configuration, if the statement is read as 'for all points'. (iii) The higher-dimensional and positive-characteristic claims, which are separate manuscripts. (iv) Whether the proof is correct: the only evidence is the authors' text and Lean files.

events.doubts: (1) The manuscript body was not read. (2) The model is unreleased and unnamed; per OpenAI, prompts and per-problem compute were not published, which the IAS advisory group's recommendations asked for (secondary summary). A press report quotes an OpenAI spokesperson that nearly every result came from a single prompt to a single agent; not verifiable. (3) Within the same release, three manuscripts in other families (Weil classes on abelian eightfolds; Kuga-Satake for K3; rational Hodge for products of K3) were withdrawn on 7 Oct 2026 for a sign error invalidating a core argument; the release has a demonstrated error rate. (4) The formal definitions of seshadriConstant and EventualMaximalSeshadri were only partly visible, so the match to the standard multi-point definition is not verified. (5) The result would resolve a conjecture for which earlier partial results gave only asymptotic or conditional statements, and no human check is public. (6) The Lean project is 'Partial progress' and 'unchecked'. (7) The Wikipedia wording names no configuration condition and no threshold; the manuscript's is 'very general' with a non-explicit threshold.
events.direction: Cuts for the conjecture: asserts the equality (the value sqrt(L^2/r)) for every sufficiently large r, at very general points, on every smooth complex projective surface and ample L.

disputes.summary: Dionne and Roth (arXiv 2406.11656, section 1.9 as read through the Cambridge excerpt) say Syzdek's Theorem 3.17 'seems to claim' that certain curves compute the Seshadri constant for odd r, a claim they say they cannot justify. Read from a summarising fetch of their text; not checked against the printed article.

The value written in Wikipedia is d/sqrt(r) with d the 'degree' of L. The literature (Hanumanthu 2016, Hanumanthu-Jacob-Suhas-Singh 2024, the OpenAI manuscript and its Lean definitions) writes sqrt(L^2/r). These agree only if d = sqrt(L^2). If d = L^2 the Wikipedia formula would exceed the standard upper bound eps <= sqrt(L^2/r). Recorded for the judging pass; not resolved here.

Wikipedia and the OpenAI manuscript name the statement the Nagata-Biran conjecture; the literature versions with an explicit threshold (r >= k_0^2 L^2) are called Nagata-Biran-Szemberg (Hanumanthu 2016 remark; Hanumanthu-Jacob-Suhas-Singh 2024 conjecture 2.5). Wikipedia's statement carries no threshold and no 'very general' condition.

summary: Searched about fifty queries across the literature, Wikipedia, the arXiv record and the AI channels, and opened the key sources (Wikipedia, the 2016-2026 Seshadri preprints, Syzdek's repository record, Dionne-Roth's Cambridge Core text, and OpenAI's repository, Lean files and manuscript header). Before 2024 the bullet's status rested on partial or conditional results: Nagata 1959 (plane case, square r); Roe 2003 (Nagata's plane conjecture implies the surface statement for surfaces with NS generated by L and L^2 a square); Hanumanthu 2016 (Picard number 1, equality within a factor sqrt((r+2)/(r+3)), asymptotic only); the 2008 primer's Theorem 6.1.10 as read through a summarising tool (equality when r >= L^2 and rL^2 is a perfect square); Syzdek 2007 (counterexamples to the assertions at small r on P1 x P1, and a conjectured lower N_0); Ran 1998 (a plane claim for non-square r, withdrawn). In-window human-authored work is restricted or conditional: Dionne-Roth 2024 (P1 x P1; the sqrt(L^2/r) equality for some classes is conditional on a nef-cone description; published in Forum of Mathematics, Sigma in 2025), Hanumanthu-Jacob-Suhas-Singh 2024 (blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces; conditional on a negative-curve classification; the unconditional content does not settle the statement), Laface-Ugaglia 2026 (one instance: P1 x P1, O(1,1), r = 10, eps = 1/sqrt(5)) and Malara et al. 2026 (a family of instances with r = 2n and L depending on n). The one event that claims the full statement is OpenAI's release of 6 October 2026 (family 039 of openai/math). Its manuscript 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces' (author line 'OpenAI'; header dated 23 September 2026) has the abstract 'This resolves positively the qualitative Nagata--Biran conjecture for surfaces', stating eps = sqrt(L^2/r) at very general r-tuples for every sufficiently large r, for every smooth integral complex projective surface and ample L. The Lean files I could read (Main.lean, Definitions.lean, Model.lean, PlaneCurves/Nagata.lean) contain no sorry, admit or axiom, and the Lean definition EventualMaximalSeshadri asserts an r_0 and closed exceptional sets Z_n of configurations, with the equality holding off them. The AI involvement is the authors' own account as far as the record goes: the README says the manuscripts were 'produced by an internal OpenAI model'; no human author is named. Close calls: (a) whether this is a settled resolution or an announced, unchecked one, since the manuscript body was not read, the Lean project is marked 'Partial progress' and 'review: unchecked', three other manuscripts in the same release were withdrawn within a day for a sign error, and no human engagement with this family was found four days after release; (b) whether the threshold matters, since the abstract's r_0 is not explicit or uniform, so the literature's Nagata-Biran-Szemberg form (r >= k_0^2 L^2) is not reached; (c) whether 'very general points' (the manuscript and Lean) or the Wikipedia wording's unqualified points is the right reading. The same family's plane manuscript, if correct, settles the plane instance for every r >= 10 and bears on the separate Nagata-on-curves bullet, which I did not research. OpenAI's 21 September 2026 announcement of more than 100 solved problems names no problems and cannot be tied to this bullet. No event in the window shows any AI system credited beyond this release; the Jacobian and Navier-Stokes claims are other bullets.
competing_reading: The strongest case against counting the OpenAI claim as a resolution: it is a claimed proof by an unnamed, unreleased model, released without prompts or per-problem compute, with its formal status marked 'Partial progress' and 'unchecked', and four days have passed with no human engagement with this family; the same release had a sign error that invalidated an argument, so the claim is 'announced, not checked', and the bullet remains open with only conditional and restricted progress. The strongest case for counting it: the abstract states the result plainly, the Lean files I could read contain no sorry, admit or axiom, and the statement it formalises matches the literature's normalisation sqrt(L^2/r); on this reading the only gaps are the explicit threshold and the 'very general' qualifier, which Wikipedia's wording does not state either way.
what_would_settle_it: (1) A written verification of 'Maximal Seshadri constants on arbitrary polarized surfaces' by algebraic geometers, in particular of the boundary-nefness and the jets, node, compression, lattice and nef sections that the main.tex inputs. (2) An audit of the Lean project: check the definitions of seshadriConstant, EventualMaximalSeshadri, Surface and selfIntersection against the standard definitions, and run an axiom check (for example #print axioms) on maximalSeshadriConstants and its full dependency closure. (3) From OpenAI or the authors: the exact quantifiers on r_0 (whether it depends only on S and L, and whether it is effective), and whether the equality holds for all configurations or only for very general ones. (4) The manuscript's arXiv or journal version, referee reports, and any published correction to the 3 withdrawn manuscripts' neighbours that might touch the same lemmas. (5) For the AI record: the prompts and transcript for this family, or an independent reproduction, which the release does not provide. (6) For the historical record: the original Nagata-Biran-Szemberg source (the 1999 Biran paper or the 2001 Szemberg text) and the primer's attribution of Theorem 6.1.10.

incomplete: (1) Family 039 manuscripts: I did not read any of the four manuscript bodies. The surface manuscript's abstract, header and author line are from build/main.tex; its section files (introduction, jets, node, compression, lattice, nef) and the PDF were not readable. The plane, higher-dimensional and positive-characteristic claims are from the family overview and Lean files only. (2) Lean: I read Main.lean, Definitions.lean (partly), Model.lean (partly) and PlaneCurves/Nagata.lean through a summarising fetch; the definitions of seshadriConstant and EventualMaximalSeshadri were not shown in full; imports were not inspected, so sorry-freeness of the full dependency closure is not established. (3) Literature: Biran 1999 (Inventiones) and Syzdek 2005 (thesis) were not opened; Szemberg 2001 is known only from Roe's abstract; the original Nagata 1959 paper was not opened; the primer's Theorem 6.1.10 was read through a summarising tool and its attribution was not checked; Dionne-Roth's full text was read only in excerpts (sections 1 to 1.9), and its sections 9 and 10 were not read; Hanumanthu-Mukhopadhyay 2016's theorem text was not readable.
